children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were posting sharp losses Friday morning, falling to the lower edge of their nearby trading range.
The November contract was down 8.60 Canadian dollars at C$820 per ton in early activity, dipping below its 20-day moving average of C$827.60 per ton.
Losses in outside markets accounted for some spillover selling pressure. Malaysian palm oil settled at its lowest levels in two months, while Chicago soyoil hit one-month lows.
Continued weakness in the Canadian dollar lent some support to canola, as the softer currency underpins crush margins.
Statistics Canada reported that 1.2 million tons of canola were crushed in August, which was down 6.4% from the previous month but up by 42.5% from the same month the previous year.
Canada exported 43,300 tons of canola during the week ended Sept. 20, reported the Canadian Grain Commission.
Crop year-to-date exports of 752,900 tons were up by 20%.
About 22,100 canola contracts had traded as of 9:47 a.m. EDT.
